status_note: Still open on main (a4d8e00342d0): [`type_classes.md` L20-L21](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/site/docs/types/type_classes.md#L20-L21) gives `fp32`/`fp64` IEEE 754's range and precision, [`functions_comparison.yaml` L23-L27](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_comparison.yaml#L23-L27) defines `equal` as `x == y`, only `index_in` has `nan_equality` ([`functions_set.yaml` L8-L28](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_set.yaml#L8-L28)), and the sort's "quality function" ([`basics.md` L64-L71](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/site/docs/relations/basics.md#L64-L71)) is defined nowhere. No existing issue; the open draft [#1322](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/pull/1322) leaves NaN in RANGE frames implementation-defined.
summary: `fp32` and `fp64` have IEEE 754's range and precision (`type_classes.md`), and `equal` is `x == y`, but nothing says how NaN and `-0.0` compare, group, sort or deduplicate. `index_in` alone has an option for it (`nan_equality`). Sorting follows the type's "quality function", which is not defined for NaN or `-0.0`.
repro: `GROUP BY x`, `DISTINCT`, a join on `x`, `ORDER BY x` and `equal(x, x)` with `x` in `{NaN, -0.0, 0.0}`.
DuckDB 2.0: one NaN, equal to itself and above `+inf`; `-0.0` sorts before `0.0`; `signbit` sees a NaN's sign.
handling: The core leaves `nan_equality`, `nan_order`, `zero_sign` and `nan_kind` open; the reference has one NaN, equal to itself and greatest, and one zero (#89).
Could be expressed as: Extend `nan_equality` to `equal`, the comparisons and the relations that compare keys, and add an option or a stated rule for NaN's place in a sort and for `-0.0`.
